title: Synchronous block on a .NET *Async() Task via .Result/.GetResult() can hang the engine
description: Chaining .Result, .GetResult(), or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() directly onto a *Async(...) call blocks the calling thread until the Task completes. In the single-threaded HttpListener engine (Start-LocalWebEngine.ps1) and on WinForms UI threads this is a sync-over-async anti-pattern: if the awaited operation never completes (for example a half-open WebSocket upgrade the client abandoned) the thread is pinned indefinitely, and repeated occurrences exhaust the thread pool and freeze the entire engine. This was the verified root cause of the 8042 engine HANG.
detection_method: Regex scan for a *Async(...) call chained directly to .Result, .GetResult(), or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() with no bounded Wait(timeout) or cancellation.
preventionRule: Do not block sync-over-async in single-threaded listeners or UI threads. Use a bounded Task.Wait(timeoutMs) with cancellation, or redesign so the operation is not accepted at all.
remedy:
# BEFORE
$ws = $ctx.AcceptWebSocketAsync($null).GetResult()

# AFTER (bounded) or reject the upgrade entirely
$t = $ctx.AcceptWebSocketAsync($null)
if (-not $t.Wait(2000)) { return }  # timeout: abandon, do not pin the thread
